D: A family Christmas goes so badly that a young boy's lost spirit summons the dark shadow of St. Nicholas.
P: Serve the gingerbread when the gingerbread men come to life.
S: the family snowed in with the power out
Crackers, cheddar and pickles pulled from the pantry, all you can manage when the power is out and the snow is up to the windows.
the relatives who cannot get along
Homemade French onion dip with chips, a peace offering for a family dinner already going wrong.
M: the tense family dinner before the storm
Beef lasagne with a bubbling cheesy top, comfort food for the night before everything goes wrong.
W: Gingerbread men iced with jagged grinning teeth, much friendlier to eat than to meet in the attic.
K: Warm spiced apple juice with cinnamon and cloves.

s.note: the family snowed in with the power out
s.how: Arrange 200g crackers, 200g sliced cheddar and a bowl of pickles on a board. Add a few candles to the table if you want the power-cut feel.

s.note: the relatives who cannot get along
s.how: Cook 2 sliced onions in 30g butter over low heat for 30 minutes until jammy. Cool, chop and stir into 250g sour cream with salt. Serve with 200g potato chips.

m.note: the tense family dinner before the storm
m.how: Brown 600g beef mince, add 700g passata and simmer 20 minutes. Make a white sauce from 40g butter, 40g flour and 500ml milk. Layer with lasagne sheets, top with 150g mozzarella and bake at 180C for 40 minutes.

w.how: Melt 100g butter with 100g golden syrup and 80g brown sugar. Mix in 300g flour and 2 tsp ginger, roll out, cut men and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Pipe on jagged grins with icing.

d.how: Heat 1.2L apple juice with 2 cinnamon sticks and 4 cloves for 15 minutes without boiling. Ladle into mugs and keep the pot warm on the stove for refills.
